subject: Insurance
title: Hazard, Peril, and Loss
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Hazard, Peril, and Loss.

hook.text: Insurers separate risk into three parts: a peril causes loss, a hazard increases the chance of a peril.

buildup.text: Fire is a peril. Storing gasoline in your garage is a hazard. Your burned-down house is the loss.

discovery.text: Hazards can be physical (old wiring), moral (intention to commit fraud).

twist.text: Morale hazard is the sneakiest. People with insurance take more risks because they're protected.

climax.text: Understanding hazard, peril, and loss lets insurers price risk precisely.

punchline.text: Peril, hazard, loss. Three words that define how insurers see every risk.

quiz.question: What is a hazard in insurance terms?
options: The financial damage from an event
A condition that increases the likelihood of a peril
